question: What was Turkan-i-Chahalgani formed by Iltutmish?

options.text: Group of transferable generals of army

solution:
The correct answer is __**Group of 40 Turkish Amirs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Turkan-i-Chahalgani, also known as the "Group of Forty," was formed by **Iltutmish**, the ruler of the Delhi Sultanate in the early 13th century.
 
• It comprised a group of **40 powerful Turkish nobles or Amirs**, who were trusted advisors and administrators under Iltutmish's reign.
 
• The primary purpose of this group was to **centralize administration** and strengthen the Sultan's control over the vast territories of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• This elite group wielded significant power and influence in the governance and decision-making processes during Iltutmish's rule.
 
• The Turkan-i-Chahalgani later became a source of internal conflict, as some members of the group sought to expand their own power at the expense of the Sultan.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Iltutmish's Contribution to the Delhi Sultanate:**

 
 
• Iltutmish is regarded as one of the most important rulers of the Slave Dynasty, consolidating and expanding the Sultanate.
 
• He introduced the silver currency known as the **Tanka** and the copper currency called **Jital**, laying the foundation for a unified monetary system.
 
 
 
• **Role of Turkish Nobles:**
 
 
• During the early Delhi Sultanate period, Turkish nobles played a crucial role in administration, military, and politics.
 
• The creation of the Turkan-i-Chahalgani was an attempt to organize and formalize their role within the Sultanate.
 
 
 
• **Challenges from Turkan-i-Chahalgani:**
 
 
• After Iltutmish's death, the Turkan-i-Chahalgani became a source of political instability due to internal rivalries and power struggles.
 
• This group significantly influenced the succession of rulers and often undermined the central authority of the Sultan.
 
 
 
• **Slave Dynasty Overview:**
 
 
• The Slave Dynasty, also known as the Mamluk Dynasty, was the first dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate, established by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
 
• Iltutmish succeeded Aibak and is credited with strengthening the Sultanate's foundation through administrative and military reforms.
